note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - New swelling of the left elbow noted by patient while in the shower; no remembered injury or trauma precipitant.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Onset approximately 1 week ago.
  - Non–life‑threatening course: not very painful overall, feels "weird" with a sense of fluid; slightly warm to touch.
  - Able to move elbow normally.
- ENT symptoms:
  - No throat swelling/closure sensation.
  - No voice change or hoarseness.
  - No dysphagia or odynophagia.
  - No drooling.
  - No nasal or ocular symptoms.
  - No stridor, noisy breathing, or dyspnea.
  - No facial, lip, tongue, or uvular swelling.
  - No ear pain, hearing changes, or neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - History of osteoarthritis diagnosed by GP a few years ago.
  - No prior similar elbow swelling reported.
  - No prior hospitalizations or injections for this problem mentioned.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergy: peanuts (severity/reaction not specified).
  - No medication allergies reported.
  - Regular medications: none reported.
  - Rescue/PRN medications/devices: none reported.
- Social/contextual details:
  - Patient is 53 years old (DOB 05 April 1973).
  - Patient confirmed being in a private place to speak; presence of another person with patient was not stated.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution:
  - Visible swelling over the left elbow (olecranon region) noted on inspection.
  - Skin over tip of elbow described as slightly warm compared with adjacent skin.
  - Skin at tip of elbow described as a bit dry.
- Airway/breathing descriptors:
  - Not applicable / no abnormalities stated.
- Mental status and associated features:
  - Patient alert, coherent; no dizziness or syncope reported.
- Vitals and examination findings:
  - Vitals: Not recorded.
  - Examination: patient can move elbow normally; pressing over tip not very tender but area adjacent to swelling feels "weird" per patient.
- Presence of another person with the patient:
  - Not recorded.

Assessment:
- Clinical impression:
  - Probable olecranon bursitis (inflammation of the bursal sac at the elbow).
- Key justifications from transcript:
  - Localized swelling at the tip of the left elbow for ~1 week, slight warmth, fluid sensation, preserved range of motion, no history of acute trauma.
  - Clinician assessed that findings do not currently suggest septic arthritis.
- Conflict noted:
  - None identified.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Start oral nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory therapy: ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food (instruction given). If patient develops heartburn, advised to stop ibuprofen.
  - Arrange blood tests: full screen including inflammatory markers, infection markers, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout evaluation. Blood test forms to be posted to patient’s home with instructions where to attend for sampling.
- Specific instructions to patient:
  - If elbow becomes very red, very painful, or redness spreads/becomes more intense, contact the service immediately and arrange a video or phone appointment with the clinic as soon as possible ("you need to get on the phone or have a video appointment with one of us as soon as possible" if worsening) — this was described as an emergency scenario.
  - Attend for blood tests when form arrives; contact clinic after tests so results can be reviewed.
- Escalation criteria / red flags:
  - New or worsening severe pain, increasing redness, spreading erythema, or signs suggesting infection/sepsis — seek urgent assessment.
- Follow-up:
  - Clinic will review blood test results (expected turnaround ~5–6 days from sampling).
  - Follow-up appointment to be arranged after bloods; can be face-to-face, phone, or video per patient preference. Patient advised to request face-to-face review if symptoms worsen.
- Other:
  - No discussion of allergy/anaphylaxis management, auto-injector, or ENT-specific follow-up was recorded.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vitals (temperature, heart rate) to help assess for systemic infection — not recorded.
  - Explicit description of local signs of infection (marked erythema, fluctuant collection) with measurement — not documented.
  - Specific blood test names and sample timing (exact panel) — described generally as "full screen" and tests for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatologic antibodies, gout but precise tests not listed.
  - Details of peanut allergy reaction history/severity and any prior anaphylaxis plan — not documented.
  - Availability of analgesia other than ibuprofen or contraindications to NSAIDs — not documented.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - None noted.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Transcript clear and audible; clinician and patient statements unambiguous for the documented elements.
